correctness.rationale: For independent uniform-volume points in the d-dimensional shell 0<=a<b, radial moments are mu_{2j}=b^{2j} d/(d+2j)(1-q^{d+2j})/(1-q^d), q=a/b. Rotational isotropy gives M2=2mu2 and M4=2mu4+(2+4/d)mu2², so their ratio Q_d(q) is the stated explicit rational function. Put q=e^{-t}. The log derivative of F_d(q)=(1-q^d)(1-q^{d+4})/(1-q^{d+2})² equals the positive central discrete second difference of g_t(s)=s/(exp(st)-1), strictly convex for s>0; hence Q_d strictly decreases for all d>=2. Its endpoint values are (d+2)(d+3)/[d(d+4)] for the solid ball and 1+1/d for zero thickness. Exact asymptotic losses have orders q^d and (1-q)^2 with coefficients (d+2)^2/[2d(d+4)] and 1/6, giving optimal inverse Hölder exponents 1/d and 1/2 in their respective regimes. Independently verified rational moments and both sharp endpoint coefficients symbolically in d=2..8; the analytic convexity supplies the all-d proof.
residual_risks: Dimension d>=2 is fixed known; uniform volume, not surface; exact population moments and not finite-sample statistics. Zero-thickness sphere only as limit.
